faqs.question: What does JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test measure?
faqs.answer: The JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test detects the most common mutation, V617F, in the JAK2 gene.

faqs.question: Why is JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose Polycythemia vera, Myelofibrosis, and Essential thrombocythemia • To evaluate the effectiveness of treatment for these conditions • To monitor disease progression

faqs.question: When is JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: • The JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test is recommended if you have symptoms suggestive of Polycythemia vera, Myelofibrosis, or Essential thrombocythemia such as unexplained fatigue, dizziness, or excessive bleeding or clotting. • It is also advised for individuals with a family history or genetic risk factors for these conditions.

faqs.question: What if the results of the JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate the presence of Polycythemia vera, Myelofibrosis, Essential thrombocythemia, or other related conditions.

faqs.question: What to expect during the JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test?
faqs.answer: During the test, a small amount of bone marrow is collected using a needle. The sample is sent to the laboratory for analysis using Real-Time PCR method.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test?
faqs.answer: • Your doctor may provide specific instructions regarding fasting or discontinuing certain medications before the test. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test?
faqs.answer: • Complete Blood Count (CBC): Evaluates various components of blood and helps diagnose blood disorders • Bone Marrow Biopsy: Assists in examining the bone marrow for abnormalities related to blood cell production • Genetic Testing: Determines other genetic mutations associated with certain myeloid disorders

faqs.question: What is the JAK-2 Mutation (CMPD) Test also known as?
What is Polycythemia vera?
faqs.answer: Polycythemia vera is a rare blood disorder characterised by the overproduction of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets in the bone marrow. It is often associated with the JAK-2 gene mutation.
